uttarapāla.p: [Uttara+pāla+a] (pu) Google Translate ⁇ တ္တ ပါ လာ မည်သော၊ he.
pn:
Uttarapāla. A Thera. He was the son of a Brahmin in Sāvatthī. When he had attained to years of discretion he saw the Twin Miracle and entered the Saṅgha. One day, amid desultory recollection, he was beset by sensual desires, but after a violent mental struggle, he arrested his evil thoughts and attained Arahant-ship.

In the time of Vipassī Buddha, he had made a bridge for the Buddha to cross (Thag.252-4; Thag-a.i.371f).

He is evidently identical with Setudāyaka of the Apadāna (ii.408).

[uttara + sīsa 1 + ka 2 ], with its head to the north ; D II 137, 13 (~aṃ mañcakaṃ paññāpehi); Ja I 391, 25 (yamakasālānaṃ antare ~e mañcake anuṭṭhānaseyyāya nipajji); — °- suve , °- sve , °- sse , ind. , the day after tomorrow ; A I 240, 5 (ajj’ eva … sve va … uttarasve …, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee uttarasse; Mp II 354, 10 : uttarasve ti tatiyadivase); Sadd 894, 24 (sve suve uttarasuve); — anuttara , mfn. , 1. having no superior; supreme, best ; Abh 694; 952; Vin III 1, 15 (so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho … ~o purisadammasārathi); D II 108, 24 (tathāgato ~aṃ dhammacakkaṃ pavatteti); M I 40, 4 (tad ~am brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ); Dhp 23 (phusanti dhīrā nibbānaṃ yogakkhemaṃ ~aṃ); Sn 179 (tvaṃ no satthā ~o); Th 830; Ja VI 318, 13* ; Ap 81, 25 ; Mil 70, 17 (bhante Nāgasena, buddho ~o ti, āma mahārāja, bhagavā ~o ti); Dhs 1293 (katame dhammā ~ā); Vism 510, 18 (~āya satiyā); — 2. not having an answer; unable to reply ; Abh 952; — duruttara , mfn. , unanswerable ;? Mil 21, 20 (Nāgaseno … duppasaho ~o); — niruttara , mfn. , 1. having no superior; best ; Ja VI 102, 2´ (etehi guṇehi ~aṃ, Ee so; Be, Se nirantaraṃ; Ce anuttaraṃ); Mp I 120, 11 (anuttaran ti ~aṃ); — 2. not having an answer; unable to reply ; Spk III 88, 19 ; Pv-a 117, 2 (so brāhmaṇo ~o tuṇhī ahosi); — sa-uttara , mfn. , having a superior; inferior ; D I 80, 9 (~aṃ vā cittaṃ ~aṃ cittan ti pajānāti) = M I 59, 34 (Ps I 280, 11 : ~an ti kāmāvacaraṃ anuttaran ti rūpārūpāvacaraṃ); Dhs 1292 (katame dhammā ~ā); Vism 410, 16 ; — sauttara-sapacchada, mfn. , with an awning and coverlet ; Ap 175, 3 (pallaṅko … sa-uttarasapacchado; Ap-a 445, 31 : saha uttaracchadena saha pacchadena sa-uttara-sapacchado, upari vitānaṃ bandhitvā āsanaṃ uttamavatthehi acchādetvā ti attho, Be, Se so; Ce pacchādanena sa-uttarisapacchado; Ee sa-uttarapacchado); — see also uttaratra, uttarā, ekuttarika ( sv eka ).
CPD: uttara-pāsaka , m. [ sa. uttara + pāśaka], the "upper loop", in which the upper hinge, i. e. a projecting pivot, of the wing of the door revolves; originally a creeper or rope (pāsaka !), later prob. a metal contri- vance, or a hole in the wall ( corresponding to the "little mortar", udukkhalikā, below ); bhitti-cchiddaṃ karitvā valliyâpi rajjuyâpi kavāṭaṃ bandhanti, undurehi pi upacikāhi pi khajjanti, khāyita-bandhanāni kavāṭāni patanti . . . anujānāmi piṭṭha-saṃghātaṃ udukkhali- kaṃ ~aṃ, Vin ll 148, 10-14 ≠ 120, 17 ; kavāṭaṃ katvā heṭṭhā udukkhale, upari ~e ca pavesetvā kataṃ pari- vattaka-dvāraṃ, Sp 281, 3 ; Rem. (uttara) pāsaka is not "the ( upper ) lintel ( of a door ) " (PED), and aggala- pāsaka is not "the quadrangular end of the bolt of a door" (SBE XX p. 106, CPD), but the "staple" into which the sliding bolt is inserted; cf. śīlāṅka's ṭīka ad Acārāṅgasūtra ll 1, 5, 2 aggala-pāsāgāṇi vā: . . . arga- la-pāsakā vā, yatrârgalâgrāṇi nikṣikpyante (Sp 1207, 23: kapi-sīsakaṃ nāma dvāra-bāhaṃ vijjhitvā tattha pavesito aggala-pāsako vuccati, "'monkey's head' is the name of the a. fixed in the door-post after piercing it" ).
NCP: masculine | uttarapaasaka an upper loop or fastening (for hanging a door) See also: uttara
